title: Her daughter wants to help with moving into a care home. Photos and a video are ready for the first evening.
meta_title: Moving Into a Care Home: Family Photos and Video | CareStreamAI
meta_description: Invite family before a move. They send captioned photos and a short video by private link, you approve them, and staff use them on the first evenings.
lede: Moving into a care home is one of the biggest changes in a person's life, and the first evenings are often the hardest for everyone. Family usually want to help, but have nowhere safe to send the things that would help staff start a conversation. CareStream gives them a private link, holds what they send for your approval, and puts only approved photos and videos in front of your team. It sits alongside your training and policy tools.

intro.heading: She arrives on Thursday. Her family have a box of pictures.
intro.sub: A scenario we see in many care settings.
intro.paragraph: Mrs Calloway is moving in on Thursday. Her daughter, Joanne, has told the manager, Bev, that her mother loves her garden in Stockport, her black and white spaniel, Bramble, and the Sunday roast she cooked for forty years. Joanne has a folder of photos on her phone and her niece has recorded a welcome. Bev knows these would give the key worker something to talk about on the first evening. But the home has no safe, tidy way to receive them, and nobody wants pictures of residents on a personal phone.

trail.text: Bev talks to Joanne about Thursday's move.
Joanne says she has photos and a welcome video to give.
The room is ready, with a framed photo on the shelf.
Joanne texts the pictures to Bev's own phone.
The key worker never sees them. Bev is on a course.
Mrs Calloway is tearful and asks to go home. Nobody knows about Bramble.
Photos are on three phones. Nobody knows which are fine to use.
“What did you do to help her settle?” You have good intentions and no record.

trail_close: The family did the right thing early. What was missing was a safe place for it to land. Here is how CareStream collects the photos and video, lets you check them, and gives your team something personal on the first evenings.

why.heading: The first few days set the tone for everything after
why.sub: A move is a lot to take in. Familiar things give staff a place to start.

cards.title: Something to talk about on night one
cards.body: Settling into a care home takes time, and a stranger asking how you are is not much to hold on to. A photo of a spaniel, or a niece saying hello, gives a carer a real question to ask.

cards.title: Care should reflect the person
cards.body: Care must meet a person's needs and reflect their preferences, and the provider must involve relevant persons in decisions about how care is carried on. Early family contribution is one practical way to show you did that.

cards.title: Personal phones are the wrong place
cards.body: Pictures of a resident on a carer's phone raise privacy questions. Regulation 10 includes ensuring the privacy of the person. A private link and an approval step give you something you can explain.

how.heading: From a private link to a photo in the key worker's hand.
how.sub: Photos and video messages are part of the resident profiles feature, in the same system as your policies and training. They are on Professional and above. See how staff use resident knowledge too.

blocks.heading: Invite the family before the move
bullets: On the resident's Family tab you fill in a name, an email and the relationship, and CareStream emails a private link. There is no account and no password
Each link takes up to 5 photos and up to 5 short videos. A photo can be up to 5MB (JPEG, PNG or WebP). A video can run up to 60 seconds
Each photo can have a caption of up to 140 characters and a note on who is in it. A video can have a title of up to 60 characters

talk.heading: The questions managers ask, and how CareStream answers them
talk.sub: Read this as a conversation. The questions are the ones we hear most.

items.q: A family want to help with moving into a care home. What can they do?
items.a: You invite them from the resident's record with their name and email. They get a private link and can send up to 5 photos, each with a caption, and up to 5 short videos. Nothing reaches staff until you have approved it.

items.q: Can we do this before the person has actually moved in?
items.a: Yes. Create the resident's record first, then send the invitation from it. The family can send before the move, and nothing reaches staff until you approve it. Approved items show only for current residents.

items.q: Does the family need an account or an app?
items.a: No. The link is the way in, with no login. Once they press Send the link is spent. If they want to add more later, you send a new link.

items.q: Can the system tell what is in a photo?
items.a: No. It never looks inside a picture and says it cannot describe one. It matches a question to the captions and notes people wrote, by meaning, so a caption saying wedding will also find married. A clear caption is what makes a photo easy to find.

items.q: Does a manager have to approve every photo?
items.a: Yes, for anything the family send. You can edit the caption, reject it, or approve it. Things you add yourself are approved at once.

items.q: Will the photos help with dementia confusion?
items.a: We would not say that. CareStream does not treat or change anything. What it gives is something personal for staff to talk about, safely, in the hub. How you use it with each person is for you and your team to judge.

items.q: What happens if she moves on or passes away?
items.a: Photos and videos leave the hub straight away, and anything still waiting is deleted. Approved files stay in private storage for the retention period, like the written profile, then are deleted with it.

items.q: Which plan is it on, and can I try it?
items.a: Resident profiles, photos and videos are on Professional and above. There is a 14 day free trial. You can create an account or book a demo and see the pricing page for the plan details.

limits.heading: Honest limits: it gathers and shows, it does not settle anyone

cards.title: Nobody has to look at a picture
cards.body: The assistant never looks inside a photo or watches a video. It only knows the caption, the title, the notes and who sent it. If a caption is vague, the photo is harder to find, so edit it when you approve.

cards.title: Nothing is automatic
cards.body: A photo or video does not reach staff by itself. A manager has to approve each family item, so someone needs to check the Approvals tab. Items nobody approves stay hidden from the team.

cards.title: It is not a care plan or a video call
cards.body: These are personal items to start conversations. CareStream does not do video calls, and the resident cannot record a reply. It makes no claim about how any person will respond.

items.q: How can family help with settling into a care home?
items.a: They can share what makes the person who they are: photos with clear captions, who is in them, and a short message in their own voice. Staff can then ask about real things, such as a pet or a holiday. Read more in our guide to the this is me document.

items.q: What should we ask a family to send before moving into a care home?
items.a: Three or four photos that show people and places that matter, with captions that say who or what they are. A short, warm message is plenty. Ask them to keep other people out of the picture unless those people are happy to be in it.

items.q: Can the assistant describe a photo?
items.a: No. It never looks inside a picture. It reads the caption and notes only.

items.q: How many photos and videos can a family send?
items.a: Up to 5 photos, each up to 5MB, and up to 5 videos on one link. Each video can be up to 60 seconds. A caption can be up to 140 characters for a photo and a title up to 60 characters for a video.

items.q: Do I have to approve every family photo?
items.a: Yes. Family photos and videos stay hidden from staff until you approve them. You can edit the caption or title first, or reject it. Anything you add yourself is approved at once.

items.q: What do the regulations say about involving family?
items.a: Under regulation 9, care must meet needs and reflect preferences, and relevant persons are involved in decisions. Where someone lacks capacity, section 4 of the Mental Capacity Act 2005 asks you to consider their past and present wishes, and, if practicable and appropriate, to consult anyone interested in their welfare. Check your own policies on consent and images.

guide.heading: How to prepare for a move using family photos
guide.lede: A few habits make the difference between a folder nobody opens and a photo that helps at eight o'clock on the first night. Ask early, ask for clear captions, and check before you approve.

sections.h3: Ask the family for a small, clear set
paragraphs: Moving into a care home is a lot for relatives too, so keep the request light. Ask for three or four photos and one short message. Tell them a caption helps staff find the right picture, and that you will read everything first.

Look at each one as a new carer would, and as the resident might feel about it. Tidy the captions so they are specific and kind. Reject anything that shows other people who might not want it shared. You can read what the law says about dignity and privacy in regulation 10.
checklist: Does the caption say who or what is in the picture?
Is the person the resident would be glad to see?
Does it show anyone else who might not want it shared?
Would a new carer know when to use it?

sections.h3: Hand over to the key worker
paragraphs: Tell the key worker what has been approved and show them how to ask the chat. Thank the family personally. A dementia awareness course helps staff see why small personal details matter.

guide.note: This page describes how the software works and is not legal advice. Check your own policies and local guidance for how you collect and share images of residents.
